question: Which of the following Mughal rulers built the imperial capital Shahjahanabad?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shahjahan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Mughal emperor **Shahjahan** built the imperial capital **Shahjahanabad**, which is present-day Old Delhi, in the year **1639**.
 
• Shahjahanabad was conceived as a **planned city**, with a focus on impressive architecture, commerce, and urban amenities.
 
• The city was surrounded by a **fortified wall**, with its centerpiece being the iconic **Red Fort** (Lal Qila), which served as the Mughal emperor's residence.
 
• The famous **Jama Masjid**, one of the largest mosques in India, was also constructed during Shahjahan's reign in Shahjahanabad.
 
• Shahjahanabad became a hub of **art, culture, and trade**, reflecting Shahjahan's vision of creating a grand imperial capital.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shahjahan’s Architectural Contributions:**

 
 
• Shahjahan is renowned for commissioning several iconic structures, including the **Taj Mahal** in Agra, built in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
 
• He is often referred to as the **“Prince of Builders”** for his significant contributions to Mughal architecture.
 
 
 
• **Red Fort:**
 
 
• The Red Fort, constructed in Shahjahanabad, served as the **political and ceremonial center of the Mughal Empire**.
 
• It is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a symbol of India's historical and cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Jama Masjid:**
 
 
• Built between 1650 and 1656, the Jama Masjid is an exemplary piece of Mughal architecture with intricate designs and grand scale.
 
• It remains a major religious site and tourist attraction in Delhi.
 
 
 
• **Urban Planning in Shahjahanabad:**
 
 
• The city was designed with **wide streets, markets (like Chandni Chowk), gardens, and residential areas**.
 
• It set a benchmark for urban development in the Mughal era.
